newsitem.title: UK: UK Lib Dems set tax plan to cut CO2 as Blair plans.
newsitem.headline: UK Lib Dems set tax plan to cut CO2 as Blair plans.

text.p: The minority Liberal Democrats, taking Prime Minister Tony Blair at his word over pledges to cut Britain's carbon dioxide emissions by 20 percent, on Wednesday presented him with a tax plan designed to achieve this.

The centrepiece of the party's proposals, handed in to 10 Downing Street by environment spokesman Matthew Taylor, is a carbon tax which would be gradually raised to 40 stg per tonne of CO2 produced by 2002.
In return it would be possible to cut the standard rate of Value Added Tax by one point and employers' national insurance contributions by 0.8 percentage points, a party document said.
The party also called for a programme of free home insulation for poorer families and a reduction in Value Added Tax on energy-saving materials.

He was referring to Blair's speech to a U.N. environmental conference at the weekend in which he pledged to cut emissions by 20 percent by 2015 to tackle global warming.

But he said the government still had not given details of how it proposed to meet this target. "The rhetoric will not save a single ice flow in the Arctic or Antarctic ...what matters is action," he said. -- London Newsroom +44 171 5427767
